pages.text: Sheds core heat outdoors. The heat it sheds becomes power.

pages.title: Linking
pages.text: Link each Coolant Port to its radiators with the $(l:power/binder)Binder$(/l), up to $(bold)16 blocks$().$(br2)Coolant links are blue and never carry power.

pages.title: Placement
pages.text: Each radiator needs $(bold)one uncovered outdoor face$(). Above 150°C coolant, it boils snow, ice and frozen air off its faces.$(br2)$(danger)Running radiators burn whatever stands on them.$()

pages.title: Output
pages.text: One radiator sheds about $(bold)12 kW$() from a 300°C core against -200°C outside. Colder outside sheds more.
Power out is the heat shed times the efficiency, which also rises as the outside gets colder.$(br2)While running, the coolant holds the core between 200°C and 280°C.
Iron bars, copper blocks and a Coolant Port.
